title: Constant matrix lattice images are classified by integral matrix cosets
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], K a topological field, A a subring with its induced topology, U a site object, and n a natural number. In the free rank-n sheaf of continuous K-valued coefficient modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define the constant lattice image of g in GL_n(K) on T over U to be all coordinate sums g b, where b is a vector of continuous A-valued functions. Equal left cosets g GL_n(A) and h GL_n(A) give equal lattice images on every test object. Conversely, if U is nonempty, equality of these images at the identity slice object implies equality of the cosets. Consequently, for nonempty U, equality of cosets is equivalent to equality of all their embedded lattice images. No positivity hypothesis on n is required.

proof.text: Right multiplication by an invertible integral matrix preserves the lattice image. Given an integral coefficient vector b for g h, change it to h b for g; finite sums and the ring map from constant integral to rational coefficients identify the coordinate expressions. Apply the inverse integral matrix for the reverse inclusion. QuotientGroup.leftRel_apply identifies equal left cosets with such right multiplication. This direction holds over empty objects as well.

proof.text: The free-sheaf coordinate projections recover each coefficient in a finite coordinate sum, since the basis inclusions and projections satisfy the Kronecker-delta identities. For each column of h, use the delta integral coefficient vector to see it in the h lattice. Equality with the g lattice supplies continuous integral coefficients expressing that column in the g basis.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), proof, pp. 59--60, constant matrices and evaluation of lattice coordinates

proof.text: If U is nonempty, choose a point x of U and evaluate each of these continuous coefficients at x. Matrix multiplication by g inverse shows that every entry of g inverse times h lies in A. Reverse the equality to prove the same for h inverse times g. The two matrices of their subtype entries in A multiply to the identity: the induced matrix ring map into K is injective and sends the products to the identity. They therefore form an invertible matrix over A whose image is g inverse times h. QuotientGroup.leftRel_apply then proves equality of the cosets.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), proof, pp. 59--60, constant matrices and evaluation of lattice coordinates

proof.text: Combine the forward direction on all test objects with the converse on the identity slice object. When n is zero the same finite-sum and invertibility calculations apply; no basis index is selected. The nonempty hypothesis is necessary for the evaluation converse: over an empty object all section images coincide, so global coset equality cannot generally be recovered.

lean.statement:
theorem matrixLatticeImage_coset_eq_iff
    (g h : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) K) (hU : Nonempty U.left) :
    (Quotient.mk _ g : integralMatrixCosets A n) = Quotient.mk _ h ↔
      ∀ T, matrixLatticeImage X K A U n g T = matrixLatticeImage X K A U n h T
